  "feasibility": {

    "answerable": [
      "Direction and magnitude of surface runoff vs. deep drainage (recharge) partitioning as clay content increases from 5% to 55%",
      "Sensitivity of infiltration capacity and saturated hydraulic conductivity (via pedotransfer of clay) on partitioning",
      "Changes in soil moisture storage and evapotranspiration feedbacks across the clay gradient"

  },
  "n_columns": 6,
  "n_justification": "One column per clay level (5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55%) to sweep the requested 5-55% range at 10% increments. All columns share identical location, forcing, vegetation, and non-clay soil settings so the only varied factor is clay fraction, isolating its effect on runoff/recharge partitioning.",
  "columns": [
    {"id": "clay05", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=5%, sand=45%, silt=50% (silt loam end-member)"},
    {"id": "clay15", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=15%, sand=45%, silt=40%"},
    {"id": "clay25", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=25%, sand=40%, silt=35%"},
    {"id": "clay35", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=35%, sand=35%, silt=30%"},
    {"id": "clay45", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=45%, sand=30%, silt=25%"},
    {"id": "clay55", "lat": 39.1, "lon": -96.6, "soil_texture": "clay=55%, sand=25%, silt=20% (clay end-member)"}
  ],
  "elm_config": {
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_START": "1980",
    "DATM_CLMNCEP_YR_END": "2018",
    "STOP_N": "39",
    "RUN_STARTDATE": "1980-01-01",
    "hist_variables": [
      "QRUNOFF",

      "QDRAI",
      "QRECHARGE",
      "QINFL",

    "Single-column (single-point) ELM configuration",

    "Pedotransfer functions in ELM soil hydrology linking clay to hydraulic properties"

feasibility.verdict: Feasible as a controlled single-column sensitivity experiment varying only soil clay fraction while holding climate, vegetation, and all other soil properties fixed.
answerable: Direction and magnitude of surface runoff vs. deep drainage (recharge) partitioning as clay content increases from 5% to 55%
Sensitivity of infiltration capacity and saturated hydraulic conductivity (via pedotransfer of clay) on partitioning
Changes in soil moisture storage and evapotranspiration feedbacks across the clay gradient
not_answerable: Real-site validation against observed runoff/recharge (no observations available)
Effects of concurrently varying sand/silt/organic matter (design isolates clay only)
Lateral/subsurface flow interactions requiring 3D subsurface (single-column limitation)

parsed.n_justification: One column per clay level (5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55%) to sweep the requested 5-55% range at 10% increments. All columns share identical location, forcing, vegetation, and non-clay soil settings so the only varied factor is clay fraction, isolating its effect on runoff/recharge partitioning.
requires_capabilities: User-modifiable surface dataset to override PCT_CLAY (and complementary sand) per column
Pedotransfer functions in ELM soil hydrology linking clay to hydraulic properties
assumptions: All columns use identical vegetation (single PFT), atmospheric forcing, and topographic/aquifer parameters; only PCT_CLAY (with sand adjusted, silt as residual) differs
Soil organic matter, color, and layer structure held constant across columns
First 5-10 years treated as spin-up/warm-up; partitioning analysis on quasi-equilibrium remaining years
Location chosen as a temperate sub-humid grassland (Konza-like, Kansas) to give a meaningful, non-saturated runoff/recharge signal; results interpreted as conceptual sensitivity, not site validation
Default ELM SIMTOP/VIC or standard surface-runoff scheme retained and held fixed across the ensemble
Silt = 100 - clay - sand, kept within valid texture-triangle bounds for each level
